exact_statement: For every Boolean sign f on a finite uniform cube, write q_S=hat f(S)^2, v=1-q_empty and I=sum_S |S|q_S. For each nonzero nonempty coefficient define d_f(S)=max{|T|:T contains S and q_T>0}, and U=sum_nonempty q_S(d_f(S)-|S|). Then hat f(S) is a multiple of 2^(1-d_f(S)) and H(f)<=2I+2U-(2-log2(e))v. Thus U<=KI implies H<=(2+2K)I, and d_f(S)<=L|S| implies H<=2LI-(2-log2(e))v. Balanced support antichains give H<=2I-2. On ordinary addressing with a address variables, d_f(S)=a+1, U=a/2, and the bound gives exactly H<=2a, while generic full-cube level counting costs Theta(a^2). These are structural-regime results, not a universal payment of U or a novelty claim.

exact_statement: For each rooted singleton-leaf partition tree T of [N] with 2 or 3 children per internal vertex, L_T(S)=1+sum_v b_v*1{S intersects C_v} is the length of an all-subset prefix code, max L_T<=3N-2, and H(f)<=Gamma_T(f)=sum_S fhat(S)^2 L_T(S). If Boolean f,g differ on input fraction rho, sqrt(Gamma_T(f))<=sqrt(Gamma_T(g))+2 sqrt(rho max L_T), and |I(f)-I(g)|<=2N rho. For complete depth-d ternary recursive majority g_d, d>=1, padded to N>=3^d bits, the explicit main/padding tree satisfies Gamma_T(g_d)<=6I(g_d)-3. Every truth-table edit f of this g_d satisfies Gamma_T(f)<=12I(f)-6+48N rho-16rho; in particular H(f)<=Gamma_T(f)<=12I(f) if N rho<=1/8. Every one-point edit satisfies H(f)<=Gamma_T(f)<=25I(f), and <=12I(f) for N>=6. For fixed d the code-cost difference under padding and one-point editing tends to zero.

exact_statement: For any finite probability law p, atom costs a_s>=log2(1/p_s) and nonnegative Kraft lengths l_s, let m be the mass where l_s<a_s. Then H(p)<=sum_s p_s min(a_s,l_s)+m log2(1/m)<=sum_s p_s min(a_s,l_s)+h2(m). For every integer a>=8, pad the Boolean addressing function with a address and 2^a private data coordinates to N=a+2^a+2 bits and flip its all-plus input, obtaining F_a. Put c_arith(S)=2(N-1) on nonempty S and infinity on empty S, c_inf(S)=log2(e)+sum_i_in_S log2(I(F_a)/Inf_i(F_a)), and c_level(S)=-log2(r_|S|)+log2 binom(N,|S|) for any probability prior r on levels. Then E_{p_Fa} min(c_arith,c_inf,c_level)/I(F_a)>=log2(a/2)/40, while H(F_a)/I(F_a)->4. The same lower bound holds for min(c_arith,c_mix), where c_mix is the length of any fixed subprobability prior mixture of the influence and level code laws. Thus no universal O(I) expected-cost bound exists for these three references; no queue-code or FEI claim is refuted.
